newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO to hold talks - diplomatic source.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO to hold talks - diplomatic source.

text.p: Israel's defence minister and a top PLO official planned to hold talks under U.S. and Egyptian auspices on Wednesday on resuming formal peace negotiations, a diplomatic source said.

Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai and PLO negotiator Nabil Shaath will meet at the residence of U.S. ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk and Egyptian ambassador Mohammad Bassiouny will also attend, said the source, who asked not to be identified.
Formal Israeli-PLO peace talks have been frozen since the right-wing government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
"This is part of ongoing meetings...to implement interim agreements," the source, who is close to the negotiations, said about Wednesday's talks.

Netanyahu has proposed moving straight into negotiations on a final peace settlement with the Palestinians rather than pursuing crisis-plagued talks on implementing outstanding elements of interim deals signed since 1993.

But the PLO demands he first halt the settlement-building at Jabal Abu Ghneim, or Har Homa, on Israeli-occupied land in East Jerusalem, before full-fledged talks can resume. Netanyahu has pledged repeatedly to press ahead with the construction.
The PLO has also been cool to Netanyahu's proposal to move into "final-status" talks before implementing a three-stage Israeli army redeployment from mostly rural areas of the West Bank.
Egypt has tried in recent months, with little apparent success, to mediate between the two sides after U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross failed to break the deadlock.
A spokesman for Mordechai declined to discuss the planned meeting on Wednesday and no PLO officials were immediately available for comment.
